topics.name: Radiation after mastectomy
topics.form: External beam chest-wall and regional-node radiation after breast surgery
topics.question: Did radiation lower return of cancer in the older trials after mastectomy with one to three positive nodes?
topics.summary: Yes. In older trials, fewer women had cancer come back with rays after breast removal. Fewer were dead from breast cancer. The gain for a person today can differ. A node sample alone is not a full stage or plan.
topics.human: A 2025 care guide says most people with cancer in nearby nodes should have rays after breast removal. Some low-risk cases can skip this care. The full case must be checked.
topics.caution: Rays can harm healthy cells near the target. Skin, lung or heart harm can occur. So can swelling and a rare second cancer. Severe chest pain or sudden severe trouble breathing needs urgent care.
topics.next_step: Ask how many nodes were checked and had cancer. Ask how large the spots were. Were drugs given first? Ask for the gain with and without rays, which areas need care, and how to deal with harm.

study_details.heading: Why radiation after breast removal?
study_details.text: Surgery can take out tissue that can be seen. Small groups of cancer cells may stay in the chest wall or nearby nodes. Rays can harm their DNA, the cell gene code. The goal is to stop those cells from making more cells.

study_details.heading: Cancer type and stage
study_details.text: The entry is for breast cancer after breast removal, called mastectomy. Cancer in nearby lymph nodes, small glands, is nearby spread. Nearby nodes alone do not mean stage IV. Stage is based on tumor size, cell traits and spread as well.

sources.label: Read how breast nodes are staged
Read how cancer stage is defined

study_details.heading: What a positive node sample means
study_details.text: A sentinel node test checks a few nodes that drain the breast first. A sample with cancer means cancer was found there. The test cannot show how many unchecked nodes have cancer. A few cells, small spots and large spots are not the same finding.

sources.label: Read how breast nodes are staged

study_details.heading: When doctors recommend it
study_details.text: The 2025 care guide says most people with cancer in nodes should have rays if surgery was done first. More nodes with cancer can mean a stronger case for rays. Some low-risk cases can skip rays after more nodes were removed. The full report is needed.

study_details.heading: If drugs came before surgery
study_details.text: Nodes that still have cancer after drugs are a reason to review rays. Nodes with no cancer found after drugs are a distinct case. The choice is based on the first extent of cancer and its response. A node sample alone is not enough to choose.

study_details.heading: What the older trials found
study_details.text: The 2014 pooled study had 1,314 women with one to three nodes with cancer. All had more nodes removed. At ten years, cancer had come back in about 34% with rays and 46% without rays. The proof is in Figure 3.

sources.label: Read the full pooled radiation trials

study_details.heading: Survival in people
study_details.text: At twenty years, about 42% had died from breast cancer with rays and 50% without rays in the older group. The result is death from breast cancer, not death from all causes. The rates are from past groups. They are not a forecast for one person.

sources.label: Read the full pooled radiation trials

study_details.heading: A newer trial asked a narrower question
study_details.text: SUPREMO tested rays to the chest wall in 1,607 people at medium risk. At ten years, about 81% with rays and 82% without rays were alive. No clear gain in life span was shown. People with cancer in nodes had more nodes removed. The trial does not settle care after only a node sample.

study_details.heading: If positive nodes became negative
study_details.text: B-51 tested people whose nodes had cancer at first, then had none found after drugs. No clear gain at five years was shown with added rays to node areas. The finding does not cover nodes that still had cancer. More years of follow-up are needed.

study_details.heading: Which areas receive radiation?
study_details.text: The plan can cover the chest wall or rebuilt breast and nearby node areas. A CT scan is used to map the targets and organs to protect. A breath hold can move the heart away. The team checks how much of the rays reach the heart and lungs.

study_details.heading: What is still open
study_details.text: Ask for the full surgery report. Ask for the size of spots in nodes, the count of nodes with cancer, and the tissue edges, called margins. Ask for ER, PR and HER2 tests. A breast care team must match the proof to the full case.

sources.label: Read how breast nodes are staged

study_details.heading: What was read
study_details.text: The full main papers for the pooled trials, SUPREMO and B-51 were read. Parts of the 2025 care guide on who should have rays and how to plan were checked. The new trials tested distinct groups and areas. A separate science reader is still needed.

topics.name: Chemotherapy
topics.form: Named cancer drug regimens in human trials
topics.summary: The MPACT trial tested two cancer drugs against one drug in people with metastatic pancreas cancer. More people were alive with the two drugs at one and two years. The two-drug group also had more nerve and blood cell harm.
topics.research: The MPACT trial tested two cancer drugs against one drug in people with metastatic pancreas cancer. More people were alive with the two drugs at one and two years. The two-drug group also had more nerve and blood cell harm.
topics.human: Chemo benefit depends on the cancer, stage, drug plan and patient group. A survival rate after trial entry is not a cure rate or a forecast for one person.
topics.caution: Chemo can cause side effects. The risks can differ by drug and person. Ask the care team about your drug plan, blood counts, infection signs and lasting harm.
topics.next_step: Which trial matches the cancer, stage and drug plan? You can compare survival and harm at the same time point. Ask what the added drug changes versus the same care without it.

topics.question: Did adding nab-paclitaxel to gemcitabine improve survival in the MPACT pancreas trial?

study_details.heading: How chemotherapy works
study_details.text: Chemo drugs can kill cancer cells or stop their growth. The drugs can also harm healthy cells that grow fast. A treatment plan may aim for cure, lower return risk, slower growth or relief of symptoms.

study_details.heading: Cancer type and stage
study_details.text: MPACT tested adults with metastatic pancreas cancer. The cancer had spread to distant sites, which is stage IV. The trial did not test early-stage cancer or people with only local spread.

sources.label: Read how cancer stage is defined

study_details.heading: What it was compared with
study_details.text: The trial had 431 people assigned to nab-paclitaxel plus gemcitabine and 430 to gemcitabine alone. Both groups had chemotherapy. The comparison was an added drug, not chemo versus no cancer care.

study_details.heading: Survival at one and two years
study_details.text: At one year after random assignment, 35% were alive with the two drugs and 22% with one drug. The gap was 13 percentage points. At two years, the rates were 9% and 4%. Proof is in Table 2.

study_details.heading: Known side effects
study_details.text: NCI says chemo side effects can include fatigue, hair loss, nausea and mouth sores. Some drugs can cause blood cell loss, infection risk, bleeding, bowel changes and nerve harm. The effects can differ by drug. Not every person has every effect.

sources.label: Read the NCI side effect guide

study_details.heading: Lasting side effects
study_details.text: Some chemo effects can last after treatment. NCI names harm to the heart, lungs, nerves, kidneys and organs needed to have children. Some drugs can raise the risk of a second cancer years after treatment.

sources.label: Read the NCI side effect guide

study_details.heading: Side effect rates in MPACT
study_details.text: Serious nerve symptoms were in 17% with two drugs and 1% with one drug. Serious fatigue rates were 17% and 7%. Low infection-fighting blood cells were in 38% and 27%. The listed events are grade 3 or higher. Proof is in Table 3.

study_details.heading: Why one survival rate cannot cover all chemo
study_details.text: TAILORx tested early breast cancer with no spread to underarm lymph nodes. The cancers were hormone-sensitive and HER2-negative. The main compared group had a gene-test score from 11 to 25. A gene score is not a cancer stage.

study_details.heading: A different breast cancer result
study_details.text: At nine years, about 94% were alive in both TAILORx groups. The comparison was hormone therapy alone versus hormone therapy plus chemo after surgery. Most in the tested gene-score group had no added gain. Some women age 50 or younger had less return of cancer with chemo.

study_details.heading: What was read
study_details.text: The full MPACT and TAILORx papers were read, including methods, results, tables and discussion. A separate science reader has not checked these entries. The 2013 and 2018 results are dated trial results, not current rates for all patients.

topics.name: Dandelion oil extract
topics.form: Oil extract requested; 2024 seed extracts, 2025 seed oil and water-based root extract are distinct forms
topics.question: Does dandelion oil extract slow tumor growth?
topics.summary: The full 2024 seed study shows lower cell-life signals in some cancer cells. The result changed with the cell type. Healthy-cell tests did not prove safety in people. The missing 2025 oil paper and the tumor-treatment question stay Open.
topics.research: The full 2024 seed study shows lower cell-life signals in some cancer cells. The result changed with the cell type. Healthy-cell tests did not prove safety in people. The missing 2025 oil paper and the tumor-treatment question stay Open.
topics.human: No human cancer benefit from the requested oil is shown by this study. An early trial permission is not a successful cancer trial.
topics.caution: The exact oil, plant part and route need a check. Do not replace cancer care with an oil based on a root study. Ask before putting new products on skin being treated with radiation.
topics.next_step: What is in the oil and how is it used? Test that exact form with a matched control. A safe level and benefit in people stay Open.

study_details.heading: Cancer type and stage
study_details.text: The 2024 seed study tested throat, cervix and colon cancer cell lines. It also used a non-cancer monkey kidney cell line. No human cancer stage was tested. The separate root paper used colon cells and mice. Neither source gives a matched human stage result for oil.

sources.label: Read how cancer stage is defined

study_details.heading: The 2024 seed study: what was tested
study_details.text: The team made 21 samples from dandelion, milk thistle and chamomile seeds. Six chosen extracts had cell tests. The samples were water-and-alcohol extracts from whole seeds or seeds left after oil was removed. Table 3 does not test the pure seed oils.

study_details.heading: How to read the cell numbers
study_details.text: CC50 is the test level that cut the cell-life signal in half. Lower means a stronger effect in this test. The unit is micrograms per milliliter. The numbers are lab results, not doses for people. MTT is a test of cell activity; it does not by itself prove how cells died.

study_details.heading: Dandelion: whole-seed cell results
study_details.text: Table 3 gives CC50 as mean plus or minus the spread: FaDu throat cancer, 347.40 ± 45.25; HeLa cervix cancer, 645.80 ± 28.14; RKO colon cancer, 974.90 ± 97.72. The non-cancer VERO kidney cells were 794.65 ± 41.08. All use micrograms per milliliter.

study_details.heading: Dandelion: seeds left after oil removal
study_details.text: Table 3 gives CC50 as mean plus or minus the spread: FaDu, 274.60 ± 26.87; HeLa, 360.20 ± 30.12; RKO, 633.95 ± 57.35. The non-cancer VERO cells were 578.15 ± 56.07. All use micrograms per milliliter. Oil removal did not make this a test of pure oil.

study_details.heading: Were all cancer cells more sensitive?
study_details.text: No, for the narrow claim that each cancer cell type was more affected than VERO. The VERO cells had a lower half-signal level than RKO with both extracts. VERO came from monkey kidneys. The study is not a test of all healthy human cells or safe use in people.

study_details.heading: Did throat cancer cells show a stronger effect?
study_details.text: Yes, in this cell test. The ratio is VERO CC50 divided by FaDu CC50. The whole-seed ratio was 2.29. The ratio after oil removal was 2.11. A ratio above one means the cancer cells reached the half-signal point first. For HeLa it was 1.23 and 1.61; for RKO it was 0.82 and 0.91.

study_details.heading: What the other plants showed
study_details.text: Table 3 keeps each plant separate. Milk thistle whole-seed ratios were 2.53, 1.89 and 1.78. The ratios after oil removal were 2.70, 2.14 and 1.87. The order is FaDu, HeLa, RKO. Chamomile ratios were below one for all three. The milk thistle result is not a dandelion result.

study_details.heading: Healthy cells in all three plants
study_details.text: VERO is the non-cancer cell line. Its CC50 was 794.65 and 578.15 for dandelion; 480.55 and 493.60 for milk thistle; 200.55 and 264.15 for chamomile. Each pair is whole seeds then seeds after oil removal, in micrograms per milliliter. A high number does not mean no harm at any level.

study_details.heading: Other cancer-cell results in Table 3
study_details.text: Milk thistle whole-seed CC50 was 190.05 for FaDu, 254.50 for HeLa and 270.55 for RKO. After oil removal it was 182.90, 230.85 and 264.15. Chamomile gave 363.90, 678.15 and 627.95; after oil removal, 293.30, 345.05 and 777.00. All use micrograms per milliliter. Full spread values are in the source.

study_details.heading: Setup, control and repeat gaps
study_details.text: Cells had extracts for 24 hours, then the MTT test. The extracts were first put in DMSO for the lab test. The lab test was not a DMSO skin mix. The main paper does not clearly give the cell-test repeat count, final DMSO level or a matched DMSO-only control. The result has those limits.

study_details.heading: What this study cannot answer
study_details.text: No tumor-bearing mice or people were tested in this study. It gives no human stage or survival rate. The study does not prove a cell-death path, a safe dose, or that the oil treats cancer. The full main paper, Table 3 and figure captions were read. The extra files were not read.

study_details.heading: A new oil lead, with a full-paper gap
study_details.text: The 2025 abstract says growth signals were lower in breast, cervix and food pipe cancer cells with seed oil. The full methods, control and repeat counts were not checked. Seed oil is not a flower soaked in another oil. The tumor question stays Open.

study_details.heading: A separate root question has an answer
study_details.text: Did the water-based root extract slow tumor growth in this mouse test? Yes. Figure 4 shows lower tumor growth than in the control group. This answer is for the root extract, not oil.

study_details.heading: What was tested
study_details.text: The mouse test used two human colon cell lines in mice with weak immune systems. Each mouse had a tumor on each side. There were four mice per group. Two tumors in one mouse are not two separate animals.

study_details.heading: What it was compared with
study_details.text: The control mice had salt water by mouth. The treated mice had the root extract by mouth. The test lasted 75 days. The paper has different wording for the schedule for the extract.

study_details.heading: What changed
study_details.text: Figure 4 shows lower tumor growth with root extract. The main text does not give a clear final group mean with a range for that result. The abstract says more than 90% growth reduction. The result is not a human cure rate.

study_details.heading: How it may work
study_details.text: Cell tests found changed death signals and damage to the cells' energy parts. Blocking one death signal did not stop the effect. More than one path may matter. Those tests do not prove that an oil has the same effect.

study_details.heading: What is still open
study_details.text: The study needs a larger repeat test, clear dosing records and better harm checks. Human treatment benefit stays Open. Root water extract, leaf products and oil are separate forms.

study_details.heading: What was read
study_details.text: The full 2024 seed main paper and the full root-water main paper were read. The 2025 seed-oil abstract was checked. Its full paper and the 1992 castor report are still missing. A separate science reader is still needed.

study_details.heading: Survival in people
study_details.text: No human cancer survival rate was measured. Mouse tumor growth and survival in people are different results.

topics.name: Fenugreek
topics.form: Food seeds and lab extracts
topics.summary: The seed extract lowered the cancer cell activity signal in the 2009 lab test. Cell death was seen with separate stains. Proof is in Figures 1 and 3. The test did not measure tumors or survival in people.
topics.research: The seed extract lowered the cancer cell activity signal in the 2009 lab test. Cell death was seen with separate stains. Proof is in Figures 1 and 3. The test did not measure tumors or survival in people.
topics.human: The filed studies did not test cancer care in people.
topics.caution: Strong extracts can lower blood sugar or cause an allergy. Food seeds are not the tested lab product.
topics.next_step: What should the next test check? What would a clear yes or no need?
topics.question: Did the seed extract slow cancer cell growth in the filed lab study?

study_details.heading: Cancer type and stage
study_details.text: The cancer finding comes from cells or animals. No human cancer stage was tested for this finding. A cell line or mouse tumor does not prove an effect at human stage I, II, III or IV.

sources.label: Read how cancer stage is defined

study_details.heading: What was tested
study_details.text: The 2009 paper used a seed extract in breast, pancreas and prostate cancer cells. Each level had three wells. The main test ran for three days.

study_details.heading: What it was compared with
study_details.text: The control cells had growth liquid and DMSO with no seed extract. The team also tested normal prostate cells and two pure plant compounds.

study_details.heading: What changed
study_details.text: The cell activity signal was lower with the extract. Separate live and dead cell stains found cancer cell death. Proof is in Figures 1 and 3. A lower activity signal alone is not a direct cell count.

study_details.heading: How it may work
study_details.text: Some cell death and growth signals changed. Some growth signals were higher even while cells died. The mix may act in more than one way. The study did not prove one cause for the effect.

study_details.heading: A second extract had mixed results
study_details.text: A 2021 breast-cell study ran three separate tests. Higher levels had a lower cell activity signal. Some lower levels had a higher signal. Proof is in Figure 3. The result can change with the extract and level.

study_details.heading: What is still open
study_details.text: Food seeds and the two lab extracts are different forms. The 2021 paper has conflicts in some test levels and animal counts. Neither paper is proof of a safe cancer treatment in people.

study_details.heading: What was read
study_details.text: The full 2009 and 2021 main papers were read. The new details include controls, test length and proof locations. A separate science reader and a matched human test are still needed.

study_details.heading: Survival in people
study_details.text: No human cancer survival rate is measured by this cell or animal finding. Cell activity and mouse tumor size are not a human survival percentage.

expert_view.identity: S-013 full PMC3095649: triplicate wells per concentration, 72-hour MTT versus medium+DMSO. Figure 1 reports dose-dependent signal loss; Figure 3 live/dead staining at 96 hours. Not direct cell-number endpoint. Normal prostate cultures do not establish systemic safety. TGF-beta methods 1 ng/ml versus results 5 ng/ml; diosgenin methods 15 mM versus micromolar elsewhere. S-014 PMC8057839 full main paper: Figure 3, three independent experiments, 48-hour MCF-7/SK-BR3 viability, low-level stimulation and higher-level inhibition; IC50 150 and 40 micrograms/ml. Later SK-BR3 dose labels conflict with the selected doses; mouse methods six/group versus Table 2 mortality denominator ten. No genetic perturbation establishes p53 necessity. No clinical efficacy.

topics.name: Castor oil
topics.form: Castor oil on skin or in packs; the 1992 extract is a separate lead
topics.summary: A 1992 paper is titled as a castor oil extract tumor test. Its full methods and results were not available in this review. That lead is worth checking. The record does not show whether skin oil or packs slow cancer.
topics.research: A 1992 paper is titled as a castor oil extract tumor test. Its full methods and results were not available in this review. That lead is worth checking. The record does not show whether skin oil or packs slow cancer.

study_details.heading: What changed
study_details.text: The cell test signal was lower with ivermectin in both cell lines. The signal shows cell activity. The signal is not a direct cell count or a test of how long people live. Proof is in Figure 2A and 2B.

study_details.heading: How it may work
study_details.text: Some hormone and growth signals changed. The study does not prove which signal caused the lower cell test result. Some drug-resistant cells had different results.

study_details.heading: What is still open
study_details.text: Can people safely reach the drug levels used in these cell tests? Human cancer benefit stays Open. The older mouse paper still has a journal concern. This study does not settle that concern.

study_details.heading: What was read
study_details.text: The full 2026 paper was read. The journal concern on the older mouse paper was also read. A separate science reader has not checked the finding.

study_details.heading: Survival in people
study_details.text: The cell and mouse findings do not measure how long people live. No human survival rate is known from those tests.

topics.summary: No gain in length of life was shown. At one year, 41% were alive with the added drug and 49% with cancer drugs alone. Tumor response was higher with the added drug. A tumor response is not the same as longer life. Proof is in the short study report and Figures 2 and 3.

topics.caution: Heart rhythm and eye risks need a medical check. Do not start this drug for cancer on your own.

study_details.heading: Cancer type and stage
study_details.text: The trial was in people with advanced or metastatic pancreas cancer. Metastatic means spread to distant sites, which is stage IV. The abstract does not give a separate survival result for each stage.

sources.label: Read how cancer stage is defined

study_details.heading: What was tested
study_details.text: The trial had 112 people with advanced pancreas cancer. Fifty-five had added hydroxychloroquine with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel. Fifty-seven had the same cancer drugs alone. The main test was survival at one year.

study_details.heading: What it was compared with
study_details.text: People were put in groups at random. The trial was open label, which means the drug plan was known. The control had no placebo pill. Results include all 112 people in their assigned groups.

study_details.heading: Did more people live for one year?
study_details.text: No clear gain was shown. At one year, 41% were alive with the added drug and 49% with cancer drugs alone. The test could not rule out chance. Proof is in the Efficacy results and Figure 3.

study_details.heading: Did more tumors respond?
study_details.text: Yes, for this separate test. Partial tumor shrinkage was seen in 21 of 55 people with the added drug and 12 of 57 without it. No complete response was reported. Proof is in Table 1. This did not lead to longer life.

study_details.heading: Side effects in the trial
study_details.text: Serious low infection-fighting blood cells were in about 43% with the added drug and 23% without it. The safety groups had 54 and 53 people. Some had nausea, nerve symptoms or vision changes. Proof is in Table 2.

study_details.heading: How it may work
study_details.text: The drug can block part of a cell waste-reuse process called autophagy. Cancer cells may use that process under stress. A possible target does not prove a survival gain.

study_details.heading: What is still open
study_details.text: Twenty-four people had no usable tumor response check. The trial was small and had no placebo. A gene test covered only 45 people and had a group imbalance. Tumor response was a second measure, not the main test.

study_details.heading: What was read
study_details.text: The full main paper was read. The old full-paper access gap is now closed. The added drug is not supported for routine use in this trial group. A separate science reader is still needed.

study_details.heading: Survival in people
study_details.text: At twelve months after trial entry, 41% were alive with added hydroxychloroquine and 49% with the same cancer drugs alone. The trial had 55 and 57 people in those groups. The rates are for the trial groups, not a personal forecast.

lessons.title: Cancer stages and care that can help
lessons.intro: Stage tells where cancer is and how far it has spread. Care also depends on the cancer type and cell tests. Beat cancer can mean cure, less return, longer life or less pain. Ask which goal a result proves.

sections.heading: Stage 0: cells have not invaded
sections.text: Changed cells stay in their first tissue layer. Breast DCIS is one example. Care can remove the changed area by surgery. Breast surgery may be followed by radiation. The goal is to prevent invasive cancer.

sources.label: Read how cancer stage is defined

sections.heading: Stage I: early invasive cancer
sections.text: Cancer has grown into tissue but is still limited in many staging systems. The exact rules can differ by cancer. Stage I colon cancer can be cured by surgery. Early breast care may add radiation or drugs based on cell tests.

sources.label: Read how cancer stage is defined

sections.heading: Stage II: more local growth or some node spread
sections.text: The tumor may be larger or reach nearby tissue or nodes. Some stage II cancers have no positive nodes. Colon care can start with surgery. Breast care can use surgery, radiation and drugs. Added treatment is based on risk.

sources.label: Read how cancer stage is defined

sections.heading: Stage III: more regional spread
sections.text: Cancer can involve more nearby nodes or tissue, but has no distant spread in these systems. Cure may still be the aim. Stage III colon care uses surgery and chemo. Locally advanced breast care can use drugs, surgery and radiation.

sources.label: Read how cancer stage is defined

sections.heading: Stage IV: spread to distant sites
sections.text: Cancer has reached distant parts of the body. Stage IV breast care is meant to slow cancer and control symptoms. Drugs may act throughout the body. Selected colon cancers with limited liver or lung spread may have surgery. Cure is not promised by a stage label.

sources.label: Read how cancer stage is defined

sections.heading: Distant spread does not always rule out cure
sections.text: Cancer types use different stage rules. Testicular germ cell cancer can be curable even with distant spread, with cisplatin-based drugs as one form of care. It uses stages I to III, not a stage IV label. Its result does not transfer to breast cancer.

sections.heading: A positive nearby node is not stage IV
sections.text: Nearby nodes are part of regional spread. Distant spread is a different finding. In breast cancer, tumor size, nodes, grade and ER, PR and HER2 tests help set the stage. Ask for the written stage and the reasons for it.

sources.label: Read how breast nodes are staged

sections.heading: Stage and grade are different
sections.text: Stage is a measure of extent and spread. Grade describes how abnormal cells look. A gene-test score is another measure. None of these is a home test. A cell dish or mouse tumor cannot be given a human cancer stage.

sources.label: Read how cancer stage is defined

sections.heading: How to check a claim that something beats cancer
sections.text: Ask whether the source shows cure, tumor shrinkage, less return or longer life. You can match the cancer, stage and treatment. Ask for the result without that treatment too. The herb and oil tests in this app do not prove cures at human stages.

sources.label: Read the full pooled radiation trials

sections.heading: What to ask at a care visit
sections.text: What is the cancer type and stage? Is the goal cure or control? What is my chance of return with and without each treatment? What harm may last? What test can show whether treatment worked?

lessons.title: Radiation: how it works, harm and recovery
lessons.intro: This guide is about breast and chest-wall rays after surgery. The beam can harm cancer and nearby healthy tissue. The goal is to gain more cancer control than harm. Benefits and risks must match the person and plan.

sections.heading: What exactly is radiation?
sections.text: Radiation is energy sent as waves or particles. Cancer treatment uses energy strong enough to damage DNA, the cell gene code. Damage can occur directly or through changed molecules inside cells. Cells with damage beyond repair stop dividing or die.

sections.heading: Why can it hurt healthy tissue?
sections.text: The beam can harm both cancer and healthy cells. The planned shape, angle and amount limit healthy exposure. Skin may not replace lost cells fast enough. Injury and swelling can lead to scar tissue or blocked fluid flow.

sections.heading: What makes harm more likely?
sections.text: The area and amount treated matter, as do prior rays, other drugs, smoking, existing heart or lung disease and healing problems. A skin dose hot spot can raise skin injury risk. A larger target can expose more healthy tissue.

sections.heading: What happens at treatment?
sections.text: A planning scan and position checks guide the beam. You may be asked to hold your breath to protect the heart. The team leaves the room but can see and hear you. External beam treatment does not leave you radioactive.

sections.heading: During care and the first weeks after
sections.text: Tiredness, soreness, swelling and red or darker skin can build up over weeks. Skin effects can keep getting worse for a short time after the last visit. Many early effects get better over weeks to months. Keep the follow-up visits.

sections.heading: Skin breakdown: what helps and what proof exists?
sections.text: Painful wet peeling needs a nurse or doctor check. Care may include special dressings, pain care and antibiotics for infection. A trial showed less wet peeling with prescribed mometasone than a plain cream. The trial was of prevention, not proof that all severe wounds healed.

sections.heading: The skin trial in numbers
sections.text: The main analysis had 124 people after mastectomy. Wet peeling was in 28 of 64 with mometasone and 40 of 60 with plain cream. Nineteen of 143 randomized people were left out. All had a skin-dose sheet called bolus. The result may differ with other plans.

sections.heading: Lung inflammation: urgent care can help
sections.text: A new cough, fever or trouble breathing needs a prompt check. Infection, blood clots, drug harm and cancer can look similar. Doctors may use scans, oxygen tests and other tests first. For lung swelling caused by rays, care may include steroids and oxygen. Severe cases need hospital care.

sources.label: Read the lung injury care guide

sections.heading: A record of lung recovery, with limits
sections.text: One study was a record review of 1,176 people after breast rays. Sixteen had a lung condition called organizing pneumonia. Lung findings were clear in fourteen during follow-up. Two had repeat flares. Care varied, and only two had steroids. The source was a record review, not proof of one cure.

sources.label: Read the full lung follow-up study

sections.heading: Lung scars: a real gap
sections.text: Lung swelling and fixed lung scars are different problems. Steroids can help swelling. They do not erase fixed scars. The lung guide says no specific treatment can undo lung scars caused by rays. Oxygen and lung rehab may help symptoms. Recovery is not assured.

sources.label: Read the lung injury care guide

sections.heading: Arm or chest swelling: control, not a proven cure
sections.text: Rays and node surgery can block fluid drainage. Early care can help limit swelling. A trained therapist may use fitted compression, gentle movement, skin care and lymph drainage. NCI says lasting lymphedema can be treated but has no known cure.

sections.heading: Heart harm: do not wait on chest pain
sections.text: Rare late heart problems can be serious. Severe chest pain, sudden severe trouble breathing or fainting needs emergency care. In the U.S., call 911. A heart attack may need urgent treatment to restore blood flow. The finding is not proof that all heart damage from rays is repaired.

sections.heading: Other lasting harm needs its own diagnosis
sections.text: Hard tissue, stiff shoulders, nerve symptoms, weak ribs or reconstruction problems may need tests and a rehab or surgical review. New pain or a lump may be injury or cancer. Care is based on the cause. There is no single repair or success rate for these problems.

sources.label: Read about lasting effects and care

sections.heading: Could a second cancer occur?
sections.text: Rare second cancers can occur years after care. A new cancer needs its own tissue test, stage and care plan. The care team may not be able to prove what caused one person's cancer. There is no detox that guarantees reversal of rays damage.

sources.label: Read about lasting effects and care

sections.heading: The worst cases and the limit of the proof
sections.text: Severe lung or heart harm can threaten life and can be fatal. Permanent disability or a second cancer can occur. Most people do not have these severe harms. Published recoveries do not prove every severe case was solved.

sources.label: Read the lung injury care guide

sections.heading: When to call the team today
sections.text: Report new cough, fever, new arm swelling, worsening pain or open wet skin. A hot red swollen area can be infection. Do not wait for the next scan. Get the team's day and night contact plan before treatment starts.

sources.label: Read the lung injury care guide

sections.heading: How the plan lowers risk
sections.text: Ask to see the heart and lung exposure, why each node area needs treatment, and whether breath hold can help. Ask how skin is checked and when a skin-dose sheet is needed. Planning lowers risk but does not remove all harm.

sections.heading: What you can do after each visit
sections.text: Use the skin care plan from the radiation care team. Ask before using oils, DMSO, herbs or new creams on the area. Keep gentle movement, rest and food intake suited to your symptoms. Keep a symptom log and bring it to follow-up.

sections.heading: What counts as solved?
sections.text: A symptom may ease while damage remains. A scan may improve while relapse risk stays. This guide labels trial evidence, record reviews and care advice. A full cure of every severe rays effect has not been shown. Those gaps stay Open.

lessons.title: Spike proteins: what you need to know
lessons.intro: This lesson is about the spike on SARS-CoV-2, the virus that causes COVID-19.

sections.heading: What is spike?
sections.text: Spike is a protein on the virus surface. It helps the virus enter a cell. Spike is not the whole virus. A lab test of spike is not the same as a test of infection.

sections.heading: Why do vaccines use it?
sections.text: COVID shots help immune cells learn to spot spike. An mRNA shot has instructions to make a spike target. The mRNA is broken down by the body. A protein shot has the target itself. These shots do not contain a live COVID virus.

sections.heading: Do COVID-19 vaccines cause cancer?
sections.text: NCI reports no evidence that COVID-19 shots cause cancer, make it return, or make it grow. A cell test alone does not prove those claims in people. NCI is the U.S. National Cancer Institute.

sections.heading: What did the isolated spike test show?
sections.text: A 2022 lab test had fewer groups of prostate cancer cells with a spike sample. The groups are called colonies. The study used one cell line. The test was not of a shot or infection. Benefit in people stays Open.

sections.heading: What did the infection study show?
sections.text: A 2025 study used mice with sleeping breast-cancer cells in the lungs. Cell growth was seen after flu or COVID infection. Human records linked COVID with cancer deaths and lung spread of breast cancer. Those links do not prove cause. The study did not test a shot or spike alone.

sources.label: Read the infection and cancer study

sections.heading: Can one alarming paper settle it?
sections.text: A 2021 paper about spike and DNA repair was retracted in 2022. The paper was withdrawn by the journal. DNA is the cell's gene code. The paper is not sound proof that COVID shots cause cancer.

sections.heading: What is useful during cancer care?
sections.text: Ask the team about infection risk and shot timing. A shot can swell lymph nodes, small glands that help fight germs. The swelling can affect some scans. Tell the scan team when and where you had the shot. New or lasting swelling needs a check.

sections.heading: Are there vaccine risks?
sections.text: Sore arms and fever can occur. Rare serious effects, including heart inflammation, are tracked. Your risks and care plan matter. Ask for current advice for your age and health, not a fixed schedule from this page.

lessons.title: Can less sugar starve cancer?
lessons.intro: Food choices can affect health. They are not a simple way to turn off a tumor.

sections.heading: What is known?
sections.text: Cancer cells use sugar, but so do healthy cells. NCI says no studies show that stopping sugar makes a cancer shrink or disappear. A healthy eating plan can help you get through care.

sections.heading: What can you do?
sections.text: Ask for food advice that fits your weight, symptoms, and treatment. Do not cut out whole food groups based only on a cancer slogan.

sources.label: Read the food and supplements guide

lessons.title: Why the exact product matters
lessons.intro: A food is not the same as an oil or a lab extract. Each form needs its own test.

sections.heading: Do forms share the same proof?
sections.text: A lab extract result does not prove that food or skin oil works the same way. The tested dose and route can differ. Use the study for the form that was tested.

sections.heading: What should you bring to a review?
sections.text: You should bring the label and study link. Tell the team what dose you use. Ask if it can affect your drugs, surgery, or tests. A natural label does not prove safety.

sources.label: Read the guide to herbs during care

lessons.title: Does more oxygen mean less cancer?
lessons.intro: Can more oxygen help? A lab test is not proof that a drink can treat cancer.

sections.heading: What does the research mean?
sections.text: Low oxygen can change tumor growth or drug response. This lab link does not mean that a drink will help. Tests in cells and tests in people are not the same.

sections.heading: What is the clear caution?
sections.text: Do not drink or inject peroxide for cancer. The liquid can burn the gut and cause dangerous gas bubbles. Call Poison Control if you swallow it. You should get advice right away.

questions.heading: What is the exact question?
questions.text: Ask one yes or no question at a time.

questions.heading: What was tested?
questions.text: Name the form, cancer model, and test conditions.

questions.heading: What was the comparison?
questions.text: Name the groups in the test. How did their results differ?

questions.heading: What was measured?
questions.text: Keep cell death, tumor growth, pain, and length of life as distinct results.

questions.heading: Where is the proof?
questions.text: Link the source. Record the test results. Did a new group get the same result?

questions.heading: What is still open?
questions.text: Keep gaps open. No proof is not a no. Ask what test comes next.
